newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France future reviewed calmly - min official.
newsitem.headline: Air France future reviewed calmly - min official.

text.p: France's new Communist transport minister told Air France boss Christian Blanc in a meeting on Monday evening that he would prefer a "public service solution" to privatisation and that there would be no rushed decisions, a transport ministry official said on Tuesday.

"(Transport Minister) Jean-Claude Gayssot made it clear to Christian Blanc that he prefers a public service solution to privatisation. Both men want an in-depth discussion on the issue of privatisation but also on the outlook for Air France in the coming years," said the official.
"It's a priority issue. It will be dealt with as quickly as possible but without rushing into things," the official said.
The two men are due to meet again "quite soon" and Gayssot also plans to meet unions and to have the matter discussed at European Union level.
"Everything can be renegotiated at European level. Jean-Calude Gayssot will examine the file to see how it can be reviewed," said the official.
The official said the decision by former prime minister Edouard Balladur was "rushed" and only bound Balladur, not Blanc, said the same official.

"Today the goal is to avoid reacting in the same way. The (European) Commission is not in a big hurry. It does not want to stir things up. Talks will be undertaken calmly and there's no reason to issue an ultimatum to anyone and provoke a crisis where there is no crisis," said the official.
